proposition: Let a_0 = 5, a_1 = 21 and a_n = 9*a_(n-1) + (-20)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 25, a_n = 4*4^n + 1*5^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: At n = 0 the closed form gives 5, matching a_0 = 5.
At n = 1 the closed form gives 21, matching a_1 = 21.
The closed form satisfies the recurrence: for every n in [0, 23], f(n+2) = 9*f(n+1) + (-20)*f(n). (expanding by b^(n+1) expanded as b^n + 1)
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 25 we have n^2 >= 2n.
Every integer n in [1, 25] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
Two base cases plus the recurrence identity give the closed form for every n in [0, 25].
